findings.critique: The promised payoff of Slab! - 'then give the orders yourself' - is locked behind 12+ fetch rounds with no way to see or choose it. The home card sells it and the About text describes it, yet a curious adult cannot reach it in a few minutes. Make the sessions a visible, tappable row (Four words / Two slabs - there! / Your orders) on the game and its end card; unlock freely or after one session.

Every game screen stops half-way down: on the phone the bottom 40-50% is blank paper before 'About ...' starts, on desktop the game is a 570 px strip with 55% empty below. That is emptiness, not restraint. Let the scene grow to fill the viewport (taller stage on phone; scene and controls at full height on desktop) with controls in thumb reach.

Three taps per call (pick, 'Bring the ...', 'Next') for a one-word order. In session 1 the stone tap should bring it (there is nothing else to set), and feedback should advance on its own or on any tap. A second tap on the selected stone does nothing - it should bring it.
The new session opens scrolled 101 px down, so the builder's call bubble - the whole task - is cut off at the top. Scroll to top on every new session and round.
'To him' in the place switch wraps to two lines and is clipped inside its pill on a 390 px phone. Shorten it ('Here') or give the control its own full-width row.

The game is 'read the room', but the room never changes: the same picture appears for the open-window round and the empty-cup round, and Rosa smiles while 'she pulls her cardigan tighter'. The clues live only in an eye-icon text list. Show the open window, the empty cup and her glance at the teapot in the picture; the text should be the fallback, not the game.

Stage drop zones are 59x24 px dashed boxes that overlap each other (front and back rows touch), and a placed object is a 35-39 px target. Too small and messy for a thumb. Use larger, non-overlapping spots (44 px or more) with clear gaps.

After success the pupil writes 'an one-way ticket' and the closing note says it applied 'an before a vowel letter' - yet it had just passed 'a university' and 'an hour' by sound. The pupil contradicts the rule it was shown, which muddles the point of the game. And 'It can be done with 1' never reveals which card; show it.

The notebook is a raw log: a flat list of every sentence the games displayed (including report sentences I never wrote), no game, no date, no meaning, no replay; Family Threads is missing. Group by game and session, show what each phrase did ('a request', 'a/an by sound'), and let a tap replay it.
The primary 'Next: Two slabs - there!' button is 30 px tall while the secondary 'Play again' is 48 px; the primary is the cramped one. Both 48 px.
A wrong 'make it true' shows a red X but never says what is wrong. One line - 'The key is on the box, not in it' - would teach the preposition at the moment of error.
Hint is a text link here but a square bulb button in every other game. Use one component.

The desktop game header 'Slab!' is about 18 px and its subtitle about 12 px, smaller than the home page body copy. No keyboard shortcuts (1-4 for stones, Enter for Bring/Next), and nothing tells desktop users either way.

rounds.top_problem: Let the user reach each game's real payoff in minutes: a visible, tappable session row in every game (starting with Slab!'s 'give the orders yourself') and one tap per answer instead of pick-Bring-Next.
rounds.cut: The 'About ...' block under every game (How to play / The idea) that sits below an empty half-screen - the end card already carries the passage and the reading; and the 'Bring the ...' confirm step in Slab! session 1.
rounds.words: The ideas are genuinely clever and the craft is warm and legible - the Cafe's 'a request made by describing the problem' teaches more in one line than most apps do in a lesson. But you hide the best game behind a dozen fetch-and-confirm rounds, leave half of every screen empty, and tell the Cafe's clues in text instead of showing them; fix those and I would ship it.

findings.critique: The picture contradicts the clues it is supposed to carry. 'You are carrying a beam. From the scaffold he can't see it clearly. He looks at it, unsure' shows the builder on the ground in the same shouting pose, no beam, no scaffold. 'She is counting the pile' shows no pile; 'A slab is sliding off the cart behind you' shows no cart and no slab. The round (same words, different job) rests on the situation, and the situation is only written. You fixed this in the Café (window shut, Rosa pouring); do the same here: draw the beam in your arms, the cart and the falling slab, the stock-keeper at a pile, and drop the eye-icon clue lines once the picture says it.

Your turn to call ~115 px between 'Plan:' and the tray; Picture Theatre ~150 px between the message and 'Choose a thing...' after Change it; Go On! ~220 px under 'Teach the pupil...' on the success screen; Family Threads ~100 px under the cards. Controls are pinned to the bottom and content floats at the top. Let the controls follow the content, or give the stage that height.

The ghost pelmet is gone, but the stage is still mostly empty wall: on phone the top 260 px is blank plaster and the box, key and cup are ~70 px objects in the bottom strip. Crop to the floor so the objects are big, and give the back row real depth (smaller, higher, a shadow on the floor).

The success state is the least crafted screen. The picture disappears and you get a title, a score line, six phrase chips and an accordion; on phone the bottom 40% is empty paper, on desktop a narrow column floats in 1440x900 of nothing.
